description: Embeddable drag-and-drop email editor SDK: JSON templates in, MJML out, framework-agnostic, with your own backend behind every storage feature. Source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT).
rules: Mount with `init({ container })` from `@templatical/editor`; `container` is a CSS selector or an element. It is framework-agnostic and ships no Vue or React component: call it from your framework's mount hook, in the browser only.

Import `@templatical/editor/style.css` next to `init()`: it loads the editor's font, and with `shadowDom: false` it is the only stylesheet. Give the container a definite height, such as `height: 100vh`, or the editor's sidebar, footer and panels clip.

Call `editor.unmount()` when the component is removed. In React, use the StrictMode-safe effect from the installation guide: when the effect was cleaned up before `init()` resolved, unmount the instance that arrives late.
Templates are JSON: a `TemplateContent` object (`{ blocks, settings }`). Read it with `editor.getContent()`, restore it with `init({ content })` or `editor.setContent()`, and store it as JSON.

Render a template to MJML with `await renderToMjml(content)` from `@templatical/renderer`, then compile the MJML to HTML on your server with the `mjml` package. The SDK bundles no MJML compiler, so `editor.toHtml()` needs a `render` provider.

Storage features are providers: plain objects passed to `init()` as `templates`, `versionHistory`, `comments`, `savedBlocks`, `media` and `testEmail`. Each is off until its key is passed, and none needs Cloud; `initCloud()` is the hosted variant.

Install `@templatical/editor` alone: it bundles Vue and `@templatical/core`, so the app needs neither. Optional peers: `@templatical/renderer` (`editor.toMjml()`), `@templatical/quality` (Issues panel), `pusher-js` (`initCloud()`).

Working apps with full code: `https://docs.templatical.com/frameworks/<page>.md` for `nextjs`, `nuxt`, `sveltekit`, `react-router` (with server routes) and `react` (Vite, no backend). The apps are in the repo's `examples/` folder.
